issues.legal_issue: The absence of provisions for solatium and interest in the compensation scheme for acquisition of previously requisitioned property does not violate the constitutional guarantee of equality.
material_facts: The land was requisitioned for a military purpose, and the owners were out of possession while the government possessed and used it.
The land was later acquired under a special statutory scheme that prescribed compensation by reference to the property's condition when it was requisitioned.
The owners had received compensation for the period during which the land was requisitioned.
The owners challenged the absence of solatium and interest by comparing the scheme with the general land-acquisition scheme.
issues.conclusion: The different compensation schemes were based on a reasonable classification, so the special scheme was not invalid under Article 14 and did not entitle the owners to solatium or interest under the general land-acquisition law.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits a classification founded on intelligible differentia that bears a rational relation to the legislation's lawful object. The Court applied Sections 30 and 31 of the Defence of India Act, 1971, and contrasted them with Sections 23(2) and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. It relied on Union of India v. Hari Krishan Khosla and Union of India v. Dhanwanti Devi, which held that solatium and interest under the Land Acquisition Act are not read into a distinct acquisition statute. It distinguished the Nagpur Improvement Trust decisions because those statutes incorporated the Land Acquisition Act's compensation scheme, unlike this self-contained scheme.

rule.if: special_requisition_acquisition_case and land_was_requisitioned_before_acquisition and government_possessed_land_during_requisition and owners_were_compensated_for_requisition and acquisition_purpose_was_limited

predicates.special_requisition_acquisition_case: The proceeding challenged the compensation scheme for property acquired after it had been requisitioned under a special statutory scheme.
predicates.land_was_requisitioned_before_acquisitio: The government requisitioned the land before later acquiring it.
predicates.government_possessed_land_during_requisi: The government possessed and used the land while it was requisitioned, leaving the owners out of possession.
predicates.owners_were_compensated_for_requisition: The owners received compensation for the period in which the land was requisitioned.
predicates.acquisition_purpose_was_limited: The statutory scheme permitted acquisition in limited circumstances connected with works constructed during requisition or excessive restoration costs.

issues.definition: When property acquired under a limited-purpose scheme was first requisitioned, possessed by the government, and compensated for during requisition, the differing compensation classification is constitutional.

issues.legal_issue: Previously paid solatium and interest need not be recovered when the particular circumstances make recovery unjust.
material_facts: The government had paid solatium and interest to the owners decades before the appeals, following a High Court ruling that the statutory scheme was invalid.
The owners had sought referral of the compensation dispute to an arbitrator, but no arbitrator had been appointed despite their demand.
The amounts sought to be recovered were small.
The government appealed against the judgment that had supported the payments.
issues.conclusion: In the peculiar circumstances, the government was directed not to recover the amounts already paid; the Court stated that this direction was not to be treated as a precedent.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the equitable approach reflected in Union of India v. Hari Krishan Khosla, which relied on Harbans Singh Shanni Devi v. Union of India in view of the prolonged failure to appoint an arbitrator. Given the old payments, the small sums, and the failure to appoint an arbitrator despite demand, the Court considered non-recovery just, while expressly limiting the direction to the particular facts.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_recovery_of_supplemental_compensation and supplemental_payments_were_already_made and payments_were_made_long_before_appeal and requested_arbitration_remained_unappointed and amounts_were_small

predicates.appeal_concerning_recovery_of_supplement: The proceeding was an appeal concerning whether the government could recover supplemental compensation already paid to landowners.
predicates.supplemental_payments_were_already_made: The government had already paid the landowners solatium and interest in addition to the basic compensation.
predicates.payments_were_made_long_before_appeal: The supplemental payments had been made many years before the appeal was decided.
predicates.requested_arbitration_remained_unappoint: The owners had requested an arbitrator, but the government had not appointed one despite their demand.
predicates.amounts_were_small: The sums the government sought to recover were small.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns recovery of supplemental payments already made long before the appeal, arbitration remained unappointed despite demand, and the sums were small, the government must not recover those payments.
